On being wrong in public

Keeping a list of my mistakes turned out to be the most useful page on this site

Hana Sato Sep 29, 2026

Three years ago I started keeping a public list of every claim I had made here that turned out to be wrong. It began as a way to keep myself honest, and it ended up changing how I write.

The first entry was embarrassing: a confident prediction about housing prices that missed by a mile. Writing it down took ten minutes and cost me a little pride, which seemed like a fair price.

Thanks for reading Margin Notes! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

What surprised me is how few of the mistakes were about facts. Most were about confidence: I was right about the direction and wrong about the size, or right about the size and wrong about the timing.

This is the post I send to every new analyst on my team. Being wrong in a way you can learn from is a skill, and nobody teaches it.
